items.stem: Explain the role of agencies at the national level that work for Health and Physical Education in schools.
items.answer: At the national level the agencies are NCERT, CBSE and the Sport Authority of India. NCERT is an apex autonomous organisation set up in 1961 by the Government of India for quality improvement of school education and teacher education, and it functions in the areas of educational research, training and development of curriculum and instructional materials for school education. Its National Curriculum Framework (NCF-2005) considers health and physical education a compulsory subject from Class I to X and an optional subject at Classes XI and XII; as a follow up, NCERT has prepared the syllabus on health and physical education, which was approved by the National Steering Committee set by the Government of India, and it contributes to the policy formulation process of the Central and State governments related to Health and Physical Education. CBSE develops curriculum for all subjects at the secondary and higher secondary levels, conducts evaluation and examination activities, organises teacher training workshops and develops resource materials; it has been preparing syllabi on Health and Physical Education, conducting competitive sport activities for schools affiliated to it and promoting the transaction of the subject at the secondary and higher secondary levels, and it has also been ensuring that Comprehensive and Continuous Evaluation is focused on health and physical education activities. The Sport Authority of India, set up by the Government of India in 1984, promotes sport in India and develops excellence by upgrading the skills of Indian sportpersons through 23 training centres and through schemes formulated for sub-junior, junior and senior levels.
grounding: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) is an apex autonomous organisation set up in 1961 by the Government of India for quality improvement of school education and teacher education.
It functions in the areas of educational research, training and development of curriculum and instructional materials for school education.
The National Curriculum Framework (NCF-2005) prepared by NCERT considers health and physical education a compulsory subject from Class I to X and optional subject at Classes XI and XII.
NCERT has prepared syllabus on health and physical education which has been approved by the National Steering Committee set by the Government of India.
It contributes to the policy formulation process of the Central and State governments related to Health and Physical Education.

The major functions of the CBSE have been to develop curriculum for all the subjects at the secondary and higher secondary levels, to conduct evaluation and examination activities, to organise teacher training workshops, to develop resource materials for teachers and students

The CBSE has been preparing syllabi on Health and Physical Education, conducting competitive sport activities for schools affiliated to it and promoting the transaction of Health and Physical Education at secondary and higher secondary levels.
It has also been ensuring that the Comprehensive and Continuous Evaluation (CCE) is focused on health and physical education activities.
Sport Authority of India (SAI) was set up by the Government of India in 1984, aimed to promote sport in India and developing excellence by upgrading the skills of the Indian sport persons.
In order to attain this objective 23 training centers spread over the entire country are functioning.
Through various schemes formulated for sub-junior, junior and senior levels, it ensures that the enthusiasm for sport is widened among different age groups of people.

items.stem: Which are the State level government agencies responsible for Health and Physical Education in schools? What roles do they play for the promotion of this subject area?
items.answer: At the state level there are government agencies for preparing curriculum, training teachers and other functionaries and evaluating the performance of students. There is a State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) in almost all the major States, and this institution is responsible for the preparation of syllabi and textbooks for all the classes at the primary and upper primary stages. In some States and Union Territories the State Institutes of Education (SIE) or the Directorates of Education perform these roles. Then there are State Boards of Education, responsible for the preparation of syllabi and textbooks and for the evaluation of students of all classes at the secondary and higher secondary stages. Under the SCERTs there are District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs), responsible for pre-service teacher education at the elementary stage, that is the primary and upper primary stages. These institutions also conduct in-service teacher training for all the subjects including the subject of Health and Physical Education, and all of them perform these roles for the subject area of Health and Physical Education as well.
grounding: We have found that there are government agencies at the state level for preparing curriculam, training teachers and other functionaries and evaluating the performance of students.
There is a State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) in almost all the major States.
This institution is responsible for preparation of syllabi and textbooks for all the classes at primary and upper primary stages.
In some of the States and Union Territories, the State Institutes of Education (SIE) or the Directorates of Education perform these roles.
All these institutions at the state level perform these roles for the subject area of Health and Physical Education also.
Then there are State Boards of Education, that are responsible for preparation of Syllabi and textbooks and evaluation of students of all classes at secondary and higher secondary stages.
These institutions also conduct in-service teacher training for all the subjects including the subject of Health and Physical Education.
Under SCERTs there are District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs) that are responsible for pre-service teacher education at the elementary stage (primary and upper primary stages).

items.stem: Write brief Notes on the following: a) Sports Authority of India (SAI), b) Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS), c) Sports Schools d) Yoga Institutions
items.answer: a) SAI: the Sport Authority of India was set up by the Government of India in 1984 to promote sport in India and develop excellence by upgrading the skills of Indian sportpersons; its main objective was to upgrade the skills of the budding sport talents in India, for which 23 training centres spread over the country are functioning. Its schemes include the National Sport Talent Contest, the Sport Projects Development Area, the Sport Hostel Scheme, the Army Boys Sport Company run with the Indian Army authorities, the SAI Training Centers (STC), Special Area Games (SAG) and Centre of Excellence, and it provides facilities like sport equipment for trainees, kit, stipend as well as coaches. b) NSNIS: after independence, on May 7, 1961 the National Institute of Sport was set up by the Government of India at the Motibagh Palace of the then Maharaja of Patiala, to develop sport in the country on scientific lines and to train coaches in different sport disciplines; on January 23, 1973 it was renamed Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sport (NSNIS). It produces high caliber coaches through its Diploma in Sport Coaching and Master Course in Sport Coaching, and presently conducts 6 courses pertaining to sport. c) Sport schools: Motilal Nehru School of Sport, RAI was founded in July 1973 by the Government of Haryana to provide excellent educational facilities with extra emphasis on sport to deserving students; besides it there are other sport schools such as G.V.Raja Sport School, Trivandrum, Maharana Pratap Sport College, Dehradun, Sport College, Lucknow and Sport School Jalandhar that cater to the development of sport in the school education sector, and there are also provisions for sport scholarships and sport hostels which prospective students can avail. d) Yoga institutions: a number of institutions are devoted to the promotion of yoga, providing everything from in depth courses to flexible drop-in classes, for example the Bihar School of Yoga, Munger, The Yoga Institute, Mumbai and the Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga, New Delhi. As the style of yoga and the approach to teaching varies at each centre, it is important to give proper thought to one's needs before approaching the institute.
grounding: Sport Authority of India (SAI) was set up by the Government of India in 1984, aimed to promote sport in India and developing excellence by upgrading the skills of the Indian sport persons.
The main objective to establish SAI was to upgrade the skills of the budding sport talents in India.
In order to attain this objective 23 training centers spread over the entire country are functioning.
Some of the SAI schemes formulated for the promotion of sport in India include National Sport Talent Contest. The Sport Projects Development Area and the Sport Hostel Scheme.
Besides, the Army Boys Sport Company (ABSC) in association with the Indian Army authorities is also run by SAI.
SAI provides facilities like sport equipment for the trainees, kit, stipend as well as coaches.
Another scheme proposed by SAI is called SAI Training Centers (STC).
Another ambicious schemes run by SAI are - Special Area Games (SAG), and Centre of excellence (COX)
After independence, on May 7, 1961 the National Institute of Sport (NIS) was set up by the Government of India for the development of sport at the Motibagh Palace of the then Maharaja of Patiala.
With the objective of developing sport in the country on scientific lines and to train the coaches in different sport disciplines.
On January 23, 1973, it was renamed as Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sport (NSNIS).
The Institute is producing high caliber coaches in sport disciplines through its Diploma in Sport Coaching and Master Course in Sport Coaching.
The Institute is presently conducting 6 courses pertaining to sport.

Another important agency is Motilal Nehru School of Sport, RAI which was founded in July 1973 by the Government of Haryana to provide excellent educational facilities with extra emphasis on sport to deserving students.

Besides this there are other sport schools such as: G.V.Raja Sport School, Trivandrum; Maharana Pratap Sport College, Dehradun, Sport College, Lucknow, Sport School Jalandhar etc. that cater to the development of sport in the school education sector.
There are also provisions for sport scholarships and sport hostels which prospective students can avail.
There are a number of institutions devoted to promotion of yoga, providing everything from in depth courses to flexible drop-in classes.
As the style of yoga and approach to teaching varies at each center, it is important to give proper thought to your needs before approaching the Institute.

items.stem: Which are the national awards that are given to sportpersons in India? What are the criteria for conferring those awards?
items.answer: Sport awards in India are presented by the Government of India to honour the players who have performed very well in their field of sport, and all the 7 awards are given on National Sport Day every year, 29 August, the birthday of hockey maestro Major Dhyanchand. They include the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, the Arjuna Award, the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Award, the Dronacharya Awards and the Dhyan Chand Award, along with the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar and the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award; very recently the sport category has also been added to the list of areas for which the Bharat Ratna is conferred. The criteria are as follows. The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna is India's highest honour given for achievement in sport: it was devised to be an overarching honour, conferred for outstanding sporting performance, whether by an individual or a team, across all sporting disciplines in a given year. The Arjuna Award, instituted in 1961, recognises outstanding achievement in games and sport; under the revised guidelines a sportperson should not only have had good performance consistently for the previous three years at the international level with excellence for the year for which the award is recommended, but should also have shown qualities of leadership, sportpersonship and a sense of discipline, and from the year 2001 it is given only in the listed categories of disciplines, which include indigenous games and sport for the physically challenged. The Dhyan Chand Award is a Life Time Achievement award given to the veteran sportpersons of India for their achievements in their respective fields of sport.
grounding: Sport awards in India are presented by the Government of India to honour the players who have performed very well in their field of sport.
All the 7 awards are given to the proud recipient on National Sport Day every year i.e. 29 August to mark and celebrate the birthday of hockey Maestro Major Dhyanchand.
These awards include the Trophy Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, Arjuna Award, the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Award, the, the Dronacharya Awards and the Dhyan Chand Award.
The RKPP award was instituted in 2009 by the Govt. of India to recognise the contribution in sport by entities other than sport persons and coaches.
The TNNAA was instituted in 1993 by the Govt. of India.
Very recently the sport category also has been added in the list of areas for which Bharat Ratna is conferred.
It is India's highest honour given for achievement in sport.
The Khel Ratna was devised to be an overarching honour, conferred for outstanding sporting performance, whether by an individual or a team, across all sporting disciplines in a given year.
The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961 by the Government of India to recognise outstanding achievement in games and sport.

According to the revised guidelines, to be eligible for the Award, a sportperson should not only have had good performance consistently for the previous three years at the international level with excellence for the year for which the Award is recommended, but should also have shown qualities of leadership, sportpersonship and a sense of discipline.
From the year 2001, the award is given only in disciplines falling under the following categories:
Indigenous Games
Sport for the Physically Challenged
The Dhyan Chand Award is a Life Time Achievement given to the veteran sportpersons of India for their achievements in their respective fields of sport.

items.stem: What awards are given to coaches and senior and retired sport persons? What are the bases of giving those awards?
items.answer: Coaches are given the Dronacharya Award, which was instituted in 1985 to honour eminent coaches who have done outstanding and meritorious work consistently with a singularity of purpose for raising the standards of sportpersons to highest performance in National and International events; it is named after Dronacharya because the best sportperson award is named the Arjuna Award and Dronacharya was the Guru of Arjuna. Senior and retired sportpersons are given the Dhyan Chand Award, a Life Time Achievement award given to the veteran sportpersons of India for their achievements in their respective fields of sport. Its main objective is to bestow honour on those sportspersons who have contributed a lot to their respective sport by their performance and who still continue to contribute to the promotion of sport after their retirement from the active sporting career.
grounding: Dronacharya Award was instituted in 1985 to honour eminent coaches who have
work consistently with a singularity of purpose for raising the standards of sportpersons to highest performance in National and International events.
As the best sportperson award is named Arjuna Award, it is appropriate that the coaching award is named after Dronacharya, as he was the Guru of Arjuna.
The Dhyan Chand Award is a Life Time Achievement given to the veteran sportpersons of India for their achievements in their respective fields of sport.

The main objective of the award is to bestow honour on those sportpersons who have contributed a lot to their respective sport by their performance and who still continue to contribute to the promotion of sport after their retirement from the active sporting career.

items.stem: Identify those educational and sport agencies that can help you in promoting your abilities and skills in games and sport and explain what kinds of contributions they can make.
items.answer: The agencies that can help a school student are CBSE, the Sport Authority of India, NSNIS Patiala, the sport schools, the yoga institutions and the colleges and departments of physical education. CBSE has been preparing syllabi on Health and Physical Education, conducting competitive sport activities for schools affiliated to it and promoting the transaction of the subject at the secondary and higher secondary levels, so it provides the competitions a school player can enter. SAI was set up to promote sport and develop excellence by upgrading the skills of Indian sportpersons: through its 23 training centres and schemes for sub-junior, junior and senior levels, such as the National Sport Talent Contest, the Sport Hostel Scheme and the SAI Training Centers, it provides facilities like sport equipment for trainees, kit, stipend as well as coaches, and it has also provided competitive exposures to talented sportpersons. Sport schools such as Motilal Nehru School of Sport, RAI provide excellent educational facilities with extra emphasis on sport to deserving students, and there are provisions for sport scholarships and sport hostels which prospective students can avail. NSNIS Patiala contributes expert coaching, as it produces high caliber coaches through its Diploma in Sport Coaching and Master Course in Sport Coaching. Yoga institutions offer everything from in depth courses to flexible drop-in classes, and besides these many colleges, faculties and departments of Physical Education and Sport under various state and central universities promote sport, games and physical education.
grounding: The CBSE has been preparing syllabi on Health and Physical Education, conducting competitive sport activities for schools affiliated to it and promoting the transaction of Health and Physical Education at secondary and higher secondary levels.
Sport Authority of India (SAI) was set up by the Government of India in 1984, aimed to promote sport in India and developing excellence by upgrading the skills of the Indian sport persons.
In order to attain this objective 23 training centers spread over the entire country are functioning.
Some of the SAI schemes formulated for the promotion of sport in India include National Sport Talent Contest. The Sport Projects Development Area and the Sport Hostel Scheme.
Another scheme proposed by SAI is called SAI Training Centers (STC).
SAI provides facilities like sport equipment for the trainees, kit, stipend as well as coaches.
SAI has also provided competitive exposures to the talented sportpersons.

Another important agency is Motilal Nehru School of Sport, RAI which was founded in July 1973 by the Government of Haryana to provide excellent educational facilities with extra emphasis on sport to deserving students.
There are also provisions for sport scholarships and sport hostels which prospective students can avail.
The Institute is producing high caliber coaches in sport disciplines through its Diploma in Sport Coaching and Master Course in Sport Coaching.
There are a number of institutions devoted to promotion of yoga, providing everything from in depth courses to flexible drop-in classes.

Besides these there are many other colleges, Faculties and Departments of Physical Education and Sport under various state and central Universities, which promotes sport, games and physical education.

items.stem: Write the full forms of MAKA, RGKR, TNNAA.
items.answer: MAKA is the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy, instituted in 1956-57 as a tool for promoting competitive sport amongst colleges and Universities. RGKR is the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, India's highest honour given for achievement in sport. TNNAA is the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award, instituted in 1993 and given to individuals for excelling in adventure activities on land, sea and air.
grounding: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAKA) Trophy
Government instituted MAKA Trophy in 1956-57 as a tool for promoting the competitive sport amongst colleges and Universities.
Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award
It is India's highest honour given for achievement in sport.
Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award
The TNNAA was instituted in 1993 by the Govt. of India.
The award is given to individual for Excelling Adventure Activities on land, Sea and Air.
